source.title: KidVis: Do Multimodal Large Language Models Possess the Visual Perceptual Capabilities of a 6-Year-Old?
source.authors: Xianfeng Wang; Kaiwei Zhang; Qi Jia; Zijian Chen; Guangtao Zhai; Xiongkuo Min

record.file_problem: The main paper text is present, but referenced Appendix A and Appendix B details are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures visual-task scores across parameter scales in three open-source model families and reports non-monotonic performance or saturation, challenging predictable scaling for this tested benchmark. It does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy loss.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are zero-shot KidVis aggregate scores across the Qwen3-VL, InternVL3.5 and LLaVA-Next size series. The paper does not fit loss power laws or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. V5 is not counted as tested because these are benchmark scores, not tests of whether a power-law loss form holds in another modality. The reported per-capability scores are not extracted: the scaling analysis concerns aggregate performance, and the table layout is flattened.
record.test_reason: The study compares zero-shot KidVis scores across released size series of three open-source MLLM families. It argues that parameter scaling does not reliably improve these scores, which bears on V6 for downstream performance versus scale. It does not train models, measure loss or fit power laws.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report a 'Scaling Law Paradox': more parameters do not reliably improve child-level visual perception scores. Qwen3-VL peaks at 8B and regresses at 30B, while InternVL3.5 and LLaVA-Next saturate. They conclude that scaling alone is insufficient and that architectural innovation is needed.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates zero-shot KidVis accuracy scores for existing multimodal models at different parameter scales; it does not train runs, measure held-out cross-entropy, fit power laws, or optimize compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling outcome differs across model families: Qwen3-VL peaks and regresses, while InternVL3.5 and LLaVA-Next are described as saturating.
record.problems: Only three open-source model families are analyzed for scaling; scores are benchmark accuracy aggregates rather than held-out loss, no uncertainty estimates are reported, and the referenced appendices are absent from the provided text.
record.rows_left_out: Table II reports separate capability scores for the models, but those dimension-specific values are not extracted because the scaling discussion and Fig. 4 concern aggregate performance; the flattened table makes the capability columns difficult to assign reliably. Proprietary-model and other single-size scores are not included because they do not form a stated parameter-scaling comparison.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute, and any power-law fit.
Effect of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss form in other modalities or regimes. Only benchmark scores are reported, not loss curves.
Relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance; any fitted or predictive trend; controlled scaling with fixed data and recipe; tasks beyond KidVis.
Fitting choices, exponents, and curves bending away from a power law.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is weak for V6. The models are released checkpoints whose training data and recipes may differ within a family, not controlled scaling runs. Each series has only 2–4 points, and no confidence intervals are given on a 500-question benchmark (50 items per task), so differences of 1–2 points may be noise. The authors' 'linear improvement' framing is not what V6 claims, since V6 concerns predictable rather than linear gains. Per-capability columns in Table II are flattened in the text; rows_left_out declares them.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens or compute; power-law fits and bottleneck conditions.
Extrapolation of small-run power-law fits to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The same power-law loss form in other modalities or training regimes; the study measures visual benchmark scores, not loss curves.

Only zero-shot scores on the KidVis visual-perception benchmark across three open-source model families are compared with parameter scale. No pretraining-loss-to-task-performance relationship or other downstream tasks are tested.
Fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, parameter-counting or fitting choices, and fitted curves bending away from a power law are not examined.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared across the Qwen3-VL size series.
rows.note: The paper reports that this series peaks at 8B and regresses at 30B; this row is the smallest listed model.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 4B and 30B models.
rows.note: The paper identifies 8B as the series’ aggregate-performance peak.

rows.subject: Qwen3-VL-30B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 8B model.
rows.note: The paper states that aggregate performance regresses from the 8B peak at 30B.
rows.check: The 30B model is labelled only '30B-Instruct'. It is likely the Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model with about 3B active parameters, which the paper does not mention, so parameter count may not be comparable with the dense 4B and 8B models. The value is still below the 4B→8B peak but above 4B.

rows.subject: InternVL3 5-4B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared across the InternVL3.5 size series.
rows.note: The model name is reproduced as printed in the table text.

rows.subject: InternVL3 5-8B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 4B model.
rows.note: The value is lower than the 4B model’s score.
rows.check: The drop is small (31.69 to 30.27, 1.4 points) and no uncertainty is reported. With 500 items it may be within noise, so the reversal is weak.

rows.subject: InternVL3 5-14B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 8B model.
rows.note: The value rises from 8B; the paper characterizes the series overall as saturating.

rows.subject: InternVL3 5-38B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 14B model.
rows.note: The paper says substantial parameter scaling in this family yields only tiny gains; this value is slightly below the 14B score.
rows.check: The change from 34.13 to 33.82 (0.3 points) is negligible. This is no change rather than a reversal.

rows.subject: llava-next-8b-hf
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared across the LLaVA-Next size series.
rows.note: The paper describes the LLaVA-Next series as showing performance saturation with scaling.

rows.subject: llava-next-72b-hf
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 8b model.
rows.note: The score rises, but the paper characterizes gains from substantial scaling in the series as tiny.
rows.check: The score rises clearly from 23.78 to 30.09 (+6.3 points), the largest gain in any series. The paper's 'tiny gains' wording describes the series as a whole, not this step.

rows.subject: llava-next-110b-hf
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated zero-shot on KidVis; aggregate score compared with the 72b model.
rows.note: The score is slightly lower than at 72b; the paper describes the series as saturating.
rows.check: The change from 30.09 to 29.78 is negligible. This is a plateau, not a reversal.

relationships.reason: The score peaks at 8B (38.58) and falls at 30B (36.27), so it is non-monotonic in stated size (R1–R3). The 30B model may be mixture-of-experts and no uncertainty is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Mean score fell from 38.58 at 8B to 36.27 at 30B, although the latter may use mixture-of-experts architecture and uncertainty was unreported.

relationships.condition: InternVL3.5 series (4B to 38B), zero-shot KidVis mean
relationships.reason: Scores move 31.69, 30.27, 34.13, 33.82: about +2 points over roughly a 10x parameter increase, and flat from 14B to 38B (R4–R7).
relationships.display_finding: InternVL3.5 scores progressed through 31.69, 30.27, 34.13 and 33.82, gaining about two points over roughly tenfold more parameters and plateauing from 14B to 38B.

relationships.reason: The score rises from 8B to 72B (23.78 to 30.09) and then plateaus at 110B (29.78) (R8–R10).
relationships.display_finding: LLaVA-Next improved from 23.78 at 8B to 30.09 at 72B, then plateaued at 29.78 for 110B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
